criteria.name: Logistics operations from the inside
criteria.anchor_5: Has held a role doing operational logistics work: documentation, customs, carrier coordination, shipment exceptions, dispatch, warehouse or port operations. The CV names specific operational artefacts or processes (Bills of Lading, DO release, carrier allocation, exception handling).
criteria.anchor_3: Worked closely alongside logistics operations teams (e.g. rollouts, onboarding operators) without doing the operational job themselves.
criteria.anchor_1: Logistics exposure only through software (APIs, integrations, dashboards built for someone else), or none.
criteria.source: Rohan, Sunita, Aditya, Meghna, Lavanya (all Exceeds). Contrast: Preetham (3PL integrations via API only, Below).

criteria.name: Direct line to the frontline
criteria.anchor_5: Personally and regularly works with the people who do the operational work (operators, clients' ops teams, carriers) with no account manager, product or support layer in between. The CV gives a specific example of something learned directly from them that changed what got built or done.
criteria.anchor_3: Structured user research (interviews, surveys) with a named user group, but occasional rather than ongoing.
criteria.anchor_1: User understanding comes through other teams, tickets or analytics only.
criteria.source: Aditya ("no account manager layer"), Rohan (field requirements "without a product layer"), Lavanya (discovery session that cut an account's tickets 60%). Contrast: Preetham (one of 12 engineers, no user contact).

criteria.name: Built the fix, got it adopted
criteria.anchor_5: Noticed a broken or manual workflow no one owned, built a fix without being asked (spreadsheet, tool, process, prototype), and it was adopted by the people doing the work - with the adoption stated (who, how many, how fast).
criteria.anchor_3: Built something useful on their own initiative, but for their own function only, or with no evidence it was adopted beyond themselves.
criteria.source: Rohan, Sunita, Lavanya, Meghna. Contrast: Vikram (PRD template for his PM team), Rahul (marketing case studies) - initiative, but not a frontline fix.

criteria.name: Owns it to closure, including failures
criteria.anchor_5: The CV describes at least one thing that went wrong or did not work and what the person did about it: a killed feature, a lost deal, an outage, a crisis handled under time pressure, a post-mortem written and followed through.
criteria.anchor_3: Describes handling incidents or fixes, but as part of a team or routine duty.
criteria.anchor_1: Only wins, responsibilities and credentials; nothing that went wrong.
criteria.source: Lavanya (killed 2 features, outage post-mortem), Aditya (lost-deal post-mortem), Meghna (overnight customs hold). Contrast: Vikram and Rahul (wins only).

criteria.name: Makes calls without cover
criteria.anchor_5: Was the sole owner of an area and made decisions others acted on without escalating (sole PM, ran a full cycle alone, no manager in the function).
criteria.anchor_3: Owned features or projects end to end inside a larger team with a manager setting direction.
criteria.source: Lavanya (sole PM; "she doesn't hedge"), Aditya (runs full enterprise cycle independently), Sunita (independent consultant). Contrast: Preetham (one of 12 in a 3,200-person company). PM TOTAL: 30 + 15 + 25 + 20 + 10 = 100%

criteria.name: Logistics operations from the inside
criteria.anchor_5: Everything in the PM 5, plus later used that operational knowledge to shape a product or system that operators actually use (moved from doing the work to building for it).
criteria.anchor_3: Operational logistics experience, but no evidence of turning it into a product or system.
criteria.anchor_1: Logistics exposure only through software, or none.
criteria.source: Rohan (CHA ops -> BL verification module), Lavanya (3PL ops -> dock scheduling product). Contrast: Preetham.

criteria.name: Direct line to the frontline
criteria.anchor_5: Works directly with operators AND has built a repeatable way for their team to stay close to them (ongoing discovery tracks, ops working sessions).
criteria.anchor_1: User understanding through other teams, tickets or analytics only.
criteria.source: Lavanya (3 parallel discovery tracks with freight forwarders), Rohan.

criteria.name: Built the fix, got it adopted
criteria.anchor_5: Built a fix for a broken workflow on their own initiative that spread beyond their own team (other teams, branches or customers adopted it).
criteria.anchor_3: Fix adopted within their own team only.
criteria.source: Lavanya (dashboard adopted by 2 other regional teams), Rohan (30 colleagues in the first month), Meghna (whole CS team).

criteria.name: Owns it to closure, including failures
criteria.anchor_5: Owned a significant failure at team or customer level (outage, lost account, killed initiative) and changed how the team works as a result - the change is stated.
criteria.anchor_3: Owned a failure personally, no lasting change described.
criteria.source: Aditya (loss post-mortem became standard practice), Lavanya (outage post-mortem, owned action items to closure).

criteria.name: Makes calls without cover
criteria.anchor_5: Has been the most senior person in their function (no one above them in product or equivalent), set direction and priorities, and others trusted and acted on their calls. Kargo's SPM reports straight to the founder with no Head of Product.
criteria.anchor_3: Sole owner of an area, but with a senior product leader above them.
criteria.anchor_1: Always worked with a manager setting direction.
criteria.source: Rohan ("comfortable as the most senior engineer in the room"), Sunita (independent consultant, "limited oversight"), Lavanya ("calls we trusted immediately"). Contrast: Preetham, Vikram (4-person PM team reporting to CTO). SPM TOTAL: 25 + 10 + 20 + 20 + 25 = 100%

guidance.how_to_score:
Score each criterion 1-5 using the anchors given (5 = strong, 3 = partial, 1 = absent).
Weighted score = sum of (score / 5 x weight). Maximum = 100.
Score only what is written in the CV. Do not infer from job titles, company names,
college, certifications or years of experience.
guidance.patterns:
Exceeds: Rohan, Sunita, Aditya, Meghna, Lavanya
Meets:   Vikram, Rahul
Below:   Preetham

PATTERN 1 - Worked inside logistics operations before their current role.
  All 5 Exceeds hires did hands-on freight / logistics operations work:
  Rohan (operations executive at a CHA firm, JNPT), Sunita (documentation at
  freight forwarders), Aditya (port services sales, worked alongside terminal
  operations), Meghna (documentation at a freight forwarder), Lavanya (carrier
  operations at a 3PL). None of the other 3 did. Preetham touched logistics
  only through APIs (3PL integrations) - from the software side, never the
  operations side. Vikram (HR tech) and Rahul (fintech / HR tech) have none.

PATTERN 2 - Saw a broken workflow nobody owned, built the fix unprompted,
  and the people doing the work adopted it.
  Rohan: Excel tracking system adopted by 12-person ops team in 2 weeks;
    weekend prototype of BL verification used by 30 colleagues in a month.
  Sunita: rebuilt the documentation intake workflow over a weekend when a
    vendor changed format; team kept it permanently.
  Lavanya: shipment visibility dashboard adopted by 2 other regional teams;
    same-day exception triage that "hadn't existed before".
  Meghna: onboarding checklist became the whole team's standard.
  Aditya: loss post-mortem became standard practice before qualification.
  Contrast: Vikram and Rahul built templates and programmes for their own
  function (PRD template, case study programme), not fixes for frontline users.

PATTERN 3 - Owns problems to closure, including their own failures.
  Lavanya killed 2 of her own features on usage data and wrote the outage
  post-mortem; Aditya documented why he lost a 4-month deal; Meghna worked a
  customs hold through the night; Sunita and Rohan fixed breakages under time
  pressure. Vikram's and Rahul's CVs contain only wins, frameworks and
  credentials - no failures, kills or crises owned.
guidance.do_not_reward:
DO NOT REWARD (present in Meets / Below profiles, absent as a differentiator)
- Certifications, MBAs, conference talks, framework names (JTBD, OKRs, Reforge)
- Scale of employer or user base on its own
- Polished outcome metrics with no operational context
Vikram's CV is the closest match to a standard PM spec and was rated Meets.
